decision.overall_recommendation: VIX gate is open, so new entries are technically permitted, but this system's own tracked performance (60 prior ranked picks, 3.3% win rate, avg return -3.05%) is very weak — treat that as a strong caution flag and size any new entries conservatively regardless of how clean these setups look. Of the three candidates, PLD is the standout: a genuine beat streak, twice-raised guidance, and a live $18.8B SEGRO acquisition give it a real catalyst behind the technical pattern. OHI is a reasonable secondary pick on its earnings-beat record but carries no fresh catalyst and a Hold-leaning analyst split. AA is the weakest of the three — two consecutive EPS misses despite a Buy rating and commodity tailwinds — and should be sized smallest or skipped given the system's poor track record.

ranked_picks.research_highlight: Prologis has beaten EPS estimates in 7 of its last 8 reported quarters (most recently 1.13 vs 0.75 est.), and IncomeGrowth shows accelerating Q2 2026 revenue/net income/EPS growth (+5.6%/+8.2%/+8.6%) after a soft Q1. News shows FY26 guidance raised twice on record leasing and AI-driven warehouse demand, plus a very recent, still-pending $18.8B acquisition of SEGRO plc that materially expands the platform.
ranked_picks.rationale: Strongest fundamentals-plus-catalyst combination of the group: a durable beat record, twice-raised guidance, and a live, market-moving M&A deal still working its way to close give this pick genuine forward drivers beyond the technical pattern alone. Buy-leaning analyst consensus (25 buy/16 hold/1 sell) supports the setup.
ranked_picks.bear_case: The pending $18.8B SEGRO deal raises leverage/dividend-payout questions (one item flags a 68.4% payout against 2026 Core FFO guidance), and Q1 2026 net income/EPS actually fell ~30% y/y, showing the growth trend isn't perfectly smooth — a stumble in integrating or financing the acquisition could weigh on the stock independent of the technical setup.

ranked_picks.research_highlight: Omega Healthcare beat EPS estimates in 3 of its last 4 reported quarters (including a large 1.19 vs 0.51 beat last quarter, though that print looks skewed by a one-off item), but IncomeGrowth is choppy (Q1 2026 net income/EPS fell ~8%/19% y/y) and analyst consensus is a more cautious "Hold" (7 buy/18 hold/3 sell) despite an A- rating score. News is mostly routine dividend-yield roundups with one cautionary piece on operator lease pressure; nothing forward-looking or material stands out.
ranked_picks.rationale: Solid recent beat rate and a very favorable stop-to-target R:R (5.0) support inclusion, but with no fresh catalyst and Hold-leaning analyst sentiment, this is a technical-plus-earnings-record pick rather than a momentum story — ranked behind PLD which has both.
ranked_picks.bear_case: The Hold-leaning consensus (3 sell ratings) and a news item flagging "operator pressure" as a variable in dividend stability point to a real, if not yet acute, risk in OHI's tenant base; the choppy quarter-to-quarter net income growth (a big net-income swing driven partly by non-recurring items) means the recent "beat" isn't necessarily indicative of a clean underlying trend.

ranked_picks.research_highlight: Alcoa missed EPS estimates in its last two reported quarters (2.12 vs 2.25 in Q2'26, 1.40 vs 1.53 in Q1'26) after beating in the two quarters prior, and EPS/net-income growth turned negative last quarter (-4.3%/-4.2%) even as revenue grew 24.2% y/y. News shows real tailwinds — a $4.1B South32 asset acquisition and aluminum prices at 4-year highs on supply disruption — alongside the two negative earnings-miss headlines and stock drops that followed each print.
ranked_picks.rationale: Aluminum-price and M&A tailwinds are real, and the Buy-rated consensus (22 buy/18 hold) with strong ROE/ROA scores keeps this in the pool, but the back-to-back EPS misses are a concrete deterioration signal that the clean technical setup doesn't offset — ranked last of the three given no fresh catalyst and a weakening beat record.
ranked_picks.bear_case: Two consecutive EPS misses despite strong headline revenue growth suggests margin/cost pressure (management itself has flagged tariff costs of ~$425M annually), and AA's high beta (1.62) makes it especially exposed if aluminum prices or tariff policy (a live, politically contingent variable per the news) reverse — this is a commodity-cyclical bet the technical pattern alone doesn't validate.
